purpose: Reconstruct the reference site's visual and interaction system for Engineering Intelligence while keeping Engineering Intelligence's own content, data and identity.

observedReference.graphDescription: Public design coverage describes the homepage as a graph-like visual diagram resembling sentence syntax, paired with a wiki-style index/dropdown on the right.
observedReference.indexBehaviour: Visitors can explore project/research entries from the index without leaving the spatial interface.

typography.referenceFamily: Brunswick Grotesque is reported by independent design-index sources.
typography.implementation: System grotesk stack. No proprietary font files copied.
typography.principle: Small, precise, low-contrast labels and compact body copy rather than dashboard-scale headings.

geometry.composition: Large pannable graph canvas with small floating index card.
geometry.graph: Hierarchical syntax-tree / mind-map structure rather than radial dashboard widgets.
geometry.card: Compact right-side index with dotted separators and minimal shadow.

engineeringIntelligenceMapping.Current systems: Active initiatives and systems already being built.
engineeringIntelligenceMapping.Venture lab: Commercial experiments and modelled venture candidates.

graphRules: Every top-level domain is a visible branch from Engineering Intelligence.
Every currently indexed item in projects/repos/prompts/ventures/learning appears as a leaf.
Top profitable companies appear as map leaves; the full 100-company list remains in the Index.
Exact text matches between repository usage and active systems, or repository names and venture stacks, create secondary semantic edges.
Clicking an Index row or node focuses the same graph object.

detail: does not navigate away from the map
interaction.responsive: Index becomes a bottom sheet on narrow screens while the map remains the primary surface.

repositoryRecon.reason: Useful layout primitive, but current graph benefits from deliberate syntax-tree composition.
Excellent large-graph renderer, excessive for current node count.
Strong graph analysis and visualisation, not required for the current lightweight renderer.
Strong interactive node UI framework. Keep in reserve if nested editable graphs or thousands of nodes become necessary.
Current example of a hierarchical portfolio mind map with fit-to-view, nested graph navigation and accessible semantic alternatives.
